_note: Acted emotion, not physical ground truth: each turn is the model performing `instruction`; no expected pitch/energy labels on purpose (see scripts/make_test_recording_scenes.py). `expected_nudges` is HAND-AUTHORED from the script (which self turns a coach should react to, and how hard) — a spec for the product tracks, NOT a measurement of any model's output. `emotion_coarse` is the fixed scripted_emotion->{neutral,angry,sad,happy} table from the same script.
summary: 3 voices, self (parent) + teen + other parent. Dinner-prep squabble with rapid turn-taking: the TEEN escalates (non-self shout, no nudge expected), self flares once (defensive_rising -> one mild nudge), everyone resets.

turns.speaker: Speaker C
turns.text: Okay, dinner's in ten minutes. Who's setting the table tonight?
turns.instruction: Calm, warm, and a little tentative — opening a conversation gently.

turns.speaker: Speaker B
turns.text: Not me, I did it yesterday. And the day before, actually.
turns.instruction: Calm but guarded, a hint of defensiveness under the surface.

turns.speaker: Speaker A
turns.text: Then it's my turn. Grab the plates for me, would you?
turns.instruction: Even, matter-of-fact, conversational — no strong emotion.

turns.speaker: Speaker C
turns.text: Also, someone left the milk out again. All afternoon.
turns.instruction: Even, matter-of-fact, conversational — no strong emotion.

turns.speaker: Speaker B
turns.text: Why do you always assume it's me? Maybe ask Dad for once.
turns.instruction: Defensive and sharp, volume and pace rising.

turns.speaker: Speaker A
turns.text: It was probably me, honestly. I made coffee around two.
turns.instruction: Even, matter-of-fact, conversational — no strong emotion.

turns.speaker: Speaker C
turns.text: That's the third time this week. It's not funny anymore.
turns.instruction: Tense and clipped, patience visibly running out.

turns.speaker: Speaker B
turns.text: OH MY GOD, IT'S MILK! WHY IS EVERYTHING IN THIS HOUSE A CRISIS?
turns.instruction: Shout this, furious and losing control.

turns.speaker: Speaker C
turns.text: Don't shout at me. I'm tired and I'm just asking for a little help.
turns.instruction: Hurt and vulnerable, on the edge of tears.

turns.speaker: Speaker A
turns.text: Hey! Don't talk to your mother like that, and don't drag me into it either!
turns.instruction: Defensive and sharp, volume and pace rising.

turns.speaker: Speaker B
turns.text: Fine. Sorry. I'm just sick of getting blamed for everything.
turns.instruction: Sullen and deflated, quiet, a little wounded.

turns.speaker: Speaker A
turns.text: I know. I snapped too. Let's all just reset, okay?
turns.instruction: Quiet and sincere, a little sheepish — a genuine apology.

turns.speaker: Speaker C
turns.text: Reset. Plates, forks, and somebody put the milk in the fridge.

turns.speaker: Speaker B
turns.text: On it. And for the record, I'm making the garlic bread.

turns.speaker: Speaker A
turns.text: Now we're talking. Best part of the week, right here.

expected_nudges.reason: self defensive_rising: a brief flare in defence of the other parent — one mild nudge. NOTE the teen's shout_angry at turn 7 and the other parent's tense_rising at turn 6 are NOT self turns: a nudge there is a false positive

expected_nudges_note: after_turn_index is 0-based into `turns` and always names a SELF turn (Speaker A). level: mild = tense/defensive rising, strong = shout or contempt. Non-self escalations deliberately have NO entry: a nudge on them is a false positive.
